$comment: The BUSY Bar's speed probe (emulator/test/speed.mjs --record) and the model fitted to it, for each firmware the emulator has: an app runs at the speed of the firmware the emulated bar runs at that moment (bar-speed.mjs). The bar of each is named by model and firmware, never by serial number: the file is in every release and in the public repository.

network.note: Requests to the internet from an app on the bar above, 2026-11-09, fetch() to the body's text: https to apps-api.busy.app and example.com took 1.28-1.70 s, http to example.com 0.09 s. tlsMs is the difference, the TLS handshake on the bar's processor; the emulator makes an https answer wait at least that long.

model.note: The bar's time for an app's work, fitted by emulator/test/speed.mjs to the times above: JS takes opMs per byte-code instruction plus allocByteMs per heap byte allocated; the bar's API answers a request in apiMs plus apiByteMs per byte of its body. After a draw's answer the app's JS before its next request counts twice, until it has taken redrawMs more: the cost of a frame of the probe's loop that its JS and its draw do not explain. Its likely cause is the GUI redrawing the display on the same processor at a higher priority than the app's JS (gui.c sets the GUI thread to FuriThreadPriorityHigh); it is not measured apart from the loop. work: instructions and heap bytes of the probe's pieces, counted in the runtime of `firmware` (afterDraw: the part that runs after a draw's answer, before the next request).

network.note: Requests to the internet from an app on the bar above, 2026-11-09, fetch() to the body's text: https to apps-api.busy.app and example.com took 1.28-1.70 s, http to example.com 0.09 s. tlsMs is the difference, the TLS handshake on the bar's processor; the emulator makes an https answer wait at least that long. Measured on firmware 1.3.1 and taken for 1.4.1 unchanged: not measured on 1.4.1.

runs.note: The fit takes the run on USB above, made as 1.3.1's was (on USB, 09.11). Three more runs on the same bar on 17.11, on Wi-Fi off USB, are kept here and not fitted: they differ from it by how the bar was connected, not by its firmware (the USB run matches 1.3.1's step, XPM and short draw).
